prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 团队周报看板（第 34 周） (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "成员" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 53px
  col 2: header "状态" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 61px
  col 3: header "本周完成" · longest unbreakable word 64px · one-line width 768px
  col 4: header "下周计划" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 1057px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 437px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 436px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

These are all candidate designs you produced, rendered in a real browser:
Design r1B: widths [74, 82, 120, 160] · table 437×1436px · row heights [39, 224, 276, 224, 250, 197, 224] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 10 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [74, 82, 135, 145] · table 437×1409px · row heights [39, 250, 250, 250, 197, 224, 197] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2A: widths [74, 82, 125, 155] · table 437×1409px · row heights [39, 250, 224, 250, 224, 224, 197] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [74, 81, 135, 146] · table 437×1409px · row heights [39, 250, 250, 250, 197, 224, 197] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [74, 82, 140, 140] · table 437×1567px · row heights [39, 276, 276, 303, 197, 250, 224] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 11 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3A: widths [74, 82, 119, 161] · table 437×1436px · row heights [39, 224, 276, 224, 250, 197, 224] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 10 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3B: widths [74, 82, 130, 150] · table 437×1383px · row heights [39, 250, 224, 250, 197, 224, 197] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r3C: widths [73, 82, 125, 156] · table 437×1409px · row heights [39, 250, 224, 250, 224, 224, 197] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 9 lines · mid-word splits 0

Decide as a designer:
- "preferred": the best design(s). Name more than one only if they are genuinely equally good.
- "acceptable": other designs a careful designer would still publish.
- "bad": designs with clear visual faults, each with the fault. If none of these is clearly bad, also return ONE deliberately bad but plausible alternative as "contrast" widths and say what is wrong with it.
- "ranges": for each column, the px range within which the preferred design stays equally good (keep other columns' proportions).
- "rationale": 2–4 concrete sentences about this table.
- "principles": observations that seem GENERAL (likely to hold for other tables) vs SPECIFIC to this case.
- "tradeoffs" and "uncertain": what reasonable designers could disagree on.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"preferred":["name"],"acceptable":["name"],"bad":[{"design":"name","why":""}],"contrast":{"widths":[int px],"why":""} or null,"ranges":[[min,max]],"rationale":"","principles":{"general":[""],"specific":[""]},"tradeoffs":"","uncertain":""}

log.raw: {"preferred":["r3B"],"acceptable":["r1B","r1C","r2A","r2B","r3A","r3C"],"bad":[{"design":"r2C","why":"下周计划列过窄，多行被切成短小片段；前三条记录尤其高，与本周完成列形成明显的不均衡，增加逐行比较的负担。"}],"contrast":null,"ranges":[[74,74],[82,82],[130,130],[150,150]],"rationale":"r3B 保留了成员姓名和状态的完整单行显示，使读者能先定位人员和风险，再横向比较完成情况与计划。两个叙述列宽度接近，但较长的下周计划得到更多空间；各行高度也较均衡，没有出现特别突兀的长单元格。它在候选中表格高度最短，但优势也来自两列文字的分布和可读性。","principles":{"general":["先为行标识和状态留出足够宽度，使读者能够快速定位记录。","按内容长度和列的作用分配宽度，并检查整行的换行和留白，不必强求等宽。","相近的总高度可能掩盖不同的行高分布和阅读节奏，应查看实际渲染。"],"specific":["本表的下周计划通常较长，适当宽于本周完成有助于控制换行。","74px 和 82px 分别容纳姓名及带彩色图标的状态，剩余宽度可用于两个叙述列。"]},"tradeoffs":"r1C 和 r2B 给本周完成更多空间，适合更重视回顾本周成果的读者；r2A 和 r3C 则更偏向下周计划。r3B 在两者之间取得较好的整体平衡。","uncertain":"范围采用保守的已验证值：只有 r3B 的精确宽度经过渲染，不能据此断言相邻像素宽度仍同样好。设计师也可能认为其他候选的特定行换行更自然。"}
